memory_update.text: VRT should remain the reference anchor for AI data-center power and thermal infrastructure, but it is high-attention and mega-cap; use it to benchmark suppliers rather than as the main underfollowed target.

POWL is a high-relevance switchgear candidate because management disclosed data-center orders and explicitly linked AI/data-center investment to medium-voltage switchgear demand; valuation/attention has moved it above the preferred USD 300M-10B hunting band.

MOD is a thermal-management candidate with direct AI/HPC cooling exposure, including liquid cooling, CDUs, chillers and a disclosed strategic hyperscale LTA; next layer should test LTA conversion and margin/capacity execution.

BELFB is the cleanest mid-cap underfollowed component candidate in this pass: power conversion, protection and high-speed interconnect exposure tied to AI/HPC data infrastructure, but revenue materiality requires verification.

Need a follow-up search for smaller US-listed transformer, busway, enclosure, pump, valve, heat-exchanger, leak-detection, commissioning and testing/certification names; many pure-play liquid-cooling assets remain private or embedded inside larger industrials.

node: Data-center power distribution, switchgear, transformers, UPS, busway, liquid cooling, pumps, cold plates, and thermal-management subcomponents
summary: Two-lane expansion for the AI data-center power/thermal node. Reference lane: Vertiv remains the obvious benchmark for integrated power, UPS, busway, CDU and liquid-cooling infrastructure. Underfollowed lane: Powell Industries, Modine, and Bel Fuse offer narrower or messier industrial/electronic-component exposures that map to medium-voltage switchgear, data-center cooling systems, rack-level power conversion, protection, and interconnect. Market-cap drift is notable: several once-small discovery names now screen above USD 10B, so later layers should test whether AI exposure is already fully priced and whether backlog/orders translate into margins.
